full_judgment:

 7. Similarly the Administrator has the power to appoint a mutwalli in certain cases under section 43 Of the Waqfs Ordinance. Any person aggrieved by such an appointment may appeal to the District Judge within a certain period and the decision of the District Judge shall be final. It has been held however that in spite of the use of the word "final" a revision thereafter lies to the High Court Division (Md. Khorshed Alam Vs. Amir Sultan Ali Haider, 21 DLR 799), 

 8A. The impugned order of the Administrator of Waqfs in the present case has been passed under section 44 of the Waqfs Ordinance. No appeal lies to the District Judge or to anywhere else against that decision of the Administrator of Waqfs. The learned District Judge, Dhaka was correct in not entertaining the revisional application against the order passed by the Administrator of Writes under section 44 of the Waqfs Ordinance; because the Administrator did not act as a subordinate Court to the Civil Court while exercising his powers under section 44 of the Waqfs Ordinance. 

 9. Mr. Md. Jamiruddin Sircar, the learned Advocate for the petitioner confronted with this difficulty submits that a direction May be given to the learned District Judge, Dhaka to treat Civil Revision Case No. 106 of 1983 as an appeal against the order of the Administrator of Waqfs under section 32(2) of the Waqfs Ordinance. He submits that the Administrator of Waqfs assumed jurisdiction in the present case admittedly under section 32 of the Waqfs Ordinance. Although he finally passed an order purportedly under section 44 of the Waqfs Ordinance, his order was basically an order of removal of the petitioner as a sole mutwalli of the concerned Waqf Estate. Mr. Sircar submits that an appeal under section 32(2) of the Waqfs Ordinance is therefore fully maintainable and he prays that in the interest of justice a direction may be given to the learned District Judge, Dhaka to convert the said revisional application into an appeal under section 32(2) of the Waqfs Ordinance. 

 10. I would have sympathetically considered the aforesaid submission of Mr. Sircar, but for the fact that the petitioner himself by his own conduct has forfeited his worthiness to claim such a relief from this Court. I find from the records of the case that the petitioner initially filed Miscellaneous Appeal No. 163 of 1983 on 22,5,83 against the order of the Administrator of Wanes dated 31.3.83. He was within time in preferring the appear under section 32(2) of the Wakfs Ordinance. But for reasons best known to him the said Miscellaneous Appeal No. 163 of 1983 was itself converted into Civil Revision Case No. 106 of 1983, obviously at the instance of the petitioner himself, and thereafter it is the petitioner who ran the risk of maintaining a revisional application against the impugned order of the Administrator of Waqfs. During the hearing of Civil Revision Case No. 106 of 1983 he could have prayed before the District Judge himself for converting the revisional application into an appeal, but he chose to contest the matter on a legal ground. 

 After having lost the legal battle it does not lie in his mouth now to pray for a conversion of the Civil Revisional Case into an appeal. The prayer is a belated one.
